scenarios.title: Choosing a course
scenarios.intro: You are talking to a student advisor at a local college about taking a new course.

nodes.text: Hi! I hear you're thinking about taking a course. What subject are you interested in, and why?
Have you studied this subject before, or would you be a complete beginner?
What did you find most challenging when you studied it before?
Starting something completely new can be difficult. What makes you feel confident that you can learn it?
Would you prefer to take the course online or in person? Why?
Many people find it hard to stay motivated when they study online. How would you keep yourself on track?
Attending classes in person takes time. How would you fit the course into your weekly schedule?
How do you think this course could help your career or your personal life?
If a friend asked whether they should join the course with you, what would you tell them?
Finally, what is one specific goal you would like to reach by the end of the course?

scenarios.title: A part-time job
scenarios.intro: You are speaking with a manager at a bookshop about a part-time job.

nodes.text: Thanks for coming in. Could you tell me a little about yourself and why you applied for this job?
Do you have any previous work experience?
What was the most useful thing you learned in that job?
That's fine. What experiences from school or daily life have prepared you for working with customers?
Imagine a customer is angry because a book they ordered hasn't arrived. What would you say to them?
Which hours would you be available to work, and could you work at weekends?
Great. Weekends can be very busy here. How do you usually handle pressure?
I understand. How would you balance this job with your other responsibilities?
What kinds of books do you enjoy, and how would you recommend one to a customer?
Before we finish, is there anything you would like to ask me about the job?

scenarios.title: Planning a trip
scenarios.intro: A friend wants to plan a short holiday with you.

nodes.text: I really need a holiday! If we could go anywhere for a week, where would you choose?
Would you rather relax on a beach or explore a busy city? Why?
Sounds peaceful. What would a perfect day at the beach look like for you?
Cities are exciting. What kind of places would you want to visit there, such as museums or markets?
How should we travel there, and why do you think that's the best option?
What kind of accommodation would you prefer, a hotel, a hostel, or an apartment?
What's one thing that could go wrong on the trip, and how could we prepare for it?
Great plan. Which local food would you most like to try there?

scenarios.title: Moving to a new city
scenarios.intro: A new neighbour is asking about your experience of living in different places.

nodes.text: Hello! I've just moved here. How long have you lived in this area?
Do you like living here, or would you prefer to live somewhere else?
What do you like most about this neighbourhood?
Interesting. Where would you rather live, and what would be better there?
What's the best way to get around here — by bus, bike, or car?
I'm trying to meet new people. What would you suggest I do?
When you moved to a new place before, what was the hardest thing to get used to?
Thank you! Is there a local restaurant or café you'd recommend?

scenarios.title: Healthy habits survey
scenarios.intro: A researcher is interviewing you about your lifestyle for a health study.

nodes.text: Thank you for taking part. How would you describe your lifestyle at the moment?
Do you do any regular exercise?
What motivates you to keep exercising, even when you are busy?
What stops you from exercising more often?
How would you describe your diet? Do you cook at home or eat out more often?
How many hours do you usually sleep, and do you think it's enough?
How do you usually deal with stress?
Last question: if you could change one habit tomorrow, what would it be?

scenarios.title: A school green project
scenarios.intro: A classmate wants your help to organise an environmental project at your school or workplace.

nodes.text: I want to start an environmental project here. What do you think is the biggest environmental problem in our area?
Why do you think people don't take that problem more seriously?
Should our project focus on recycling or on reducing energy use?
How could we encourage people to recycle correctly instead of putting everything in one bin?
What practical changes could people make to use less energy every day?
How should we measure whether the project is actually working?
Some people might say this project is a waste of time. How would you respond?
Who else should we ask to get involved, and why?
Imagine the project is a success. What would you like to see change in a year's time?

scenarios.title: Planning a celebration
scenarios.intro: Your cousin is helping you plan a celebration for a family member.

nodes.text: We need to plan the party for grandma's birthday. Where do you think we should have it?
Should it be a small family dinner or a big party with lots of guests?
Good idea. What food should we cook for the dinner?
A big party needs a lot of organising. What tasks should we share between family members?
What present do you think she would like most?
Can you tell me about a family celebration you remember well?
Finally, how can we make sure grandma feels really special on the day?

scenarios.title: Buying a new laptop
scenarios.intro: A shop assistant is helping you choose a new laptop.

nodes.text: Good afternoon! What will you mainly use your new laptop for?
What problems did you have with your previous computer, if any?
Is price your most important factor, or are you willing to pay more for quality?
Understood. Which features would you be willing to give up to keep the price low?
Great. Which premium features matter most to you, and why?
Do you think people replace their devices too often these days? Why or why not?
Would you consider buying a second-hand or refurbished laptop instead?
Before you decide, what questions would you like to ask me about the warranty or support?
